# fleet-hooks

Fleet git hooks: a **fail-closed credential key-scan pre-commit** plus one-command setup.

This productizes the SuperInstance fleet's house practice from the wave-52 receipts:
before every push, staged files were hand-scanned with `rg "ghp_|gho_|github_pat_"`.
That practice is now self-enforcing — the repository refuses any commit whose staged
content contains credential-shaped strings.

## Install (one-liner, run at the root of the repo you are protecting)

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/SuperInstance/fleet-hooks /tmp/fleet-hooks \
  && cp -r /tmp/fleet-hooks/.githooks . \
  && sh /tmp/fleet-hooks/setup.sh && rm -rf /tmp/fleet-hooks
```

`setup.sh` verifies the hook exists, marks it executable, sets `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`,
runs a smoke scan of your current index, and refuses (fail-closed) to arm a hooks path
that has no hook behind it. Verify any time with `git config core.hooksPath` (expect `.githooks`).

## What it scans

| class    | pattern                        | catches                                  |
|----------|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| GHP      | `ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}`          | GitHub classic personal access tokens    |
| GHO      | `gho_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}`          | GitHub OAuth tokens                      |
| GHS      | `ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}`          | GitHub App/server tokens                 |
| GHU      | `ghu_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}`          | GitHub user-to-server tokens             |
| GH_PAT   | `github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{22,}` | GitHub fine-grained personal tokens      |
| SK_ANT   | Anthropic key prefix (dash-terminated; exact pattern in the hook) | Anthropic API keys |
| AWS_KEY  | `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`             | AWS access key IDs                       |

The README spells the Anthropic prefix without its trailing dash on purpose: the
literal would make this repository fail its own gate. The hook source uses the
equivalent one-character-class spelling (`[s]k-ant-`, standard self-scan idiom)
with a comment — the class matches the identical strings.

## Design law

1. **Fail-closed.** Unknown is blocked: any scan error (git failure, unreadable
   state, pathological filename) blocks the commit with exit 2. Exit codes:
   `0` pass / nothing staged, `1` credential-shaped string found, `2` hook error.
2. **Scans the index, not the worktree.** `git grep --cached` reads exactly the
   staged blobs — what would actually be committed. A staged-then-deleted file
   cannot slip through.
3. **Deletions excluded** (nothing new to leak); typechanges out of scope.
4. **Binary blobs skipped** (`-I`) — a documented, receipted blind spot (test C4b):
   a credential inside a binary blob is not detected. Graceful, never a crash.
5. **Never echoes matched content.** The report shows class + file:line only, so
   the hook cannot leak the secret into terminals or CI logs.
6. **`.git/*` and `node_modules/*` excluded defensively** (test C9).
7. **No network, stdlib-only, POSIX sh** — needs only `sh`, `git`, `grep`, `awk`,
   `mktemp`, `wc`, `tr`, `sed`. The hook never phones home and never needs your
   real token; do not wire secrets into the hook.
8. **Escape hatch `FLEET_ALLOW`** — an environment variable holding an extended
   regex; lines that *also* match it are exempt (e.g. `FLEET_ALLOW='FAKE'` for an
   obviously-fake fixture like `ghp_` + 36 lowercase x's). Per-invocation and
   visible in shell history / CI logs — deliberately loud. Line-granular.
9. **Pathological filenames fail closed.** A staged filename containing control
   characters (git C-quotes it — e.g. an embedded newline) is refused rather than
   misparsed or silently skipped (test C8).

## Tests

```sh
sh tests/test_hooks.sh
```

11/11 controls pass (2026-09-29, dash `/bin/sh`, git 2.47.3, Linux): positive
(fake `ghp_` staged → BLOCKED, multi-class file → BLOCKED), negative (clean → PASS,
deletion → PASS, binary → PASS), escape hatch (`FLEET_ALLOW` → PASS), edge cases
(binary-with-token graceful skip, newline filename fail-closed, `node_modules`
exclusion), and setup (`setup.sh` arms a fresh repo; refuses without `.githooks`).
All fixtures are built at runtime from obviously-fake characters — the source tree
contains no credential-shaped literals, so this repo passes its own gate.

## Fleet provenance

- Codifies the wave-52 house practice: `rg "ghp_|gho_|github_pat_"` on staged files
  before every push (see the SuperInstance fleet worklog, waves 51–52 receipts).
- Seeded to `SuperInstance/quilt` (branch `hooks-53/key-scan`) so the practice is
  self-enforcing there; minimal diff: `.githooks/pre-commit` + `setup.sh`.
- House laws honored: zero force-push, append-only, honest FAIL receipts, commit
  identity `SuperInstance <fleet@superinstance.dev>`.

## Known limits (honest)

- The pattern list is prefix-classes, not exhaustive: other providers, encodings
  (base64/URL-encoded secrets), and generic high-entropy strings are not detected.
- Binary blobs are skipped (limit 4 above).
- `FLEET_ALLOW` is only as narrow as the regex you give it — prefer naming an
  obviously-fake marker (`FAKE`, `fixture`) over a broad pattern.
- Filenames containing control characters are blocked, not scanned.
fleet-hooks-main/setup.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# fleet-hooks setup — arm the fail-closed credential key-scan pre-commit
# in the repository you run it from (run at any depth inside that repo).
#
# Requires .githooks/pre-commit to exist at the repo root first (vendor it:
# see README "Install"). Fail-closed: if the hook file is missing we do NOT
# arm a hooksPath that would silently disable scanning.
#
# Exit codes: 0 armed (smoke pass), 1 setup failure, propagates the hook's
# own exit code (1/2) if the smoke run finds staged credential-shaped strings
# — that is the hook working correctly on a dirty index.

set -eu

git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "fleet-hooks setup: FAIL: not inside a git repository" >&2
  exit 1
}

root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)

if [ ! -f "$root/.githooks/pre-commit" ]; then
  echo "fleet-hooks setup: FAIL: $root/.githooks/pre-commit not found." >&2
  echo "  Vendor it first, e.g.:" >&2
  echo "    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/SuperInstance/fleet-hooks /tmp/fleet-hooks && cp -r /tmp/fleet-hooks/.githooks . && rm -rf /tmp/fleet-hooks" >&2
  echo "  Refusing to arm core.hooksPath at a path with no hook (fail-closed)." >&2
  exit 1
fi

chmod +x "$root/.githooks/pre-commit"
git config core.hooksPath .githooks

echo "fleet-hooks: armed."
echo "  repo:          $root"
echo "  core.hooksPath $(git config core.hooksPath)"
echo "  pre-commit:    fail-closed credential key-scan (ghp_/gho_/ghs_/ghu_, github_pat_, sk-ant prefix, AKIA)"
echo "  escape hatch:  FLEET_ALLOW=<ERE>  (per-invocation, loud — only for obviously-fake fixtures)"
echo "  verify:        git config core.hooksPath   # -> .githooks"

# smoke: run the hook against the current index right now
printf 'fleet-hooks: smoke — scanning current index ...\n'
sh "$root/.githooks/pre-commit"
printf 'fleet-hooks: smoke PASS (index clean or nothing staged).\n'
